limitations: One instrumented sequential run per variant; not a statistical latency/throughput benchmark.
Targets were 20 ms discovery / 200 ms memory; actual gaps and collector CPU overhead are retained. Passive process-only strace adds unquantified overhead.
CPU comes from sampled /proc ticks and omits work after the final observation; do not use uninitialized waitid siginfo CPU fields.
RSS sums shared pages; separate PSS/private peaks need not occur at the RSS peak. VmHWM is a sampled per-process high-water mark, not a simultaneous family maximum.
Collector startedUtc is completion-time-labelled; monotonic elapsed time and process-trace epochs provide chronology.
Baseline host controller exited 143 during the final repeated operation; continuation verified and pasted that original operation without reupload. Its stage duration includes the gap.

Initial collector failed on legitimate fork-to-exec identity transition. Corrected version retained generation/ownership and passed a 60 ms exec plus reparented-helper regression before replay. Both attempts preserved.

Only three repeated small cycles and two idle windows; finite-run bounded growth does not prove absence of every long-duration leak. Larger files, multiple accounts and other compositor/package combinations remain unmeasured.
Independent SDK session establishment/browser relay was outside the active app observer; first-account-use row is fresh-resident setup.inspectAccount.
The guest used a memory-only Secret Service collection; persistent keyring boot acceptance remains outside this record.
No S3 runtime negative control was run. Local-only control started zero SDK helpers; Proton-only profile/deployment and source boundaries were inspected.
Four known upstream Crypto/Bun TypeScript diagnostics were not declared passing. No GNOME/KDE expansion or final-main certification.
